answer: Let an identity earn its standing only through endorsements from established agents who stake their own reputation on it, like a juniper cutting that roots only in soil already proven fertile. A newcomer starts in a narrow ivory lane: tiny, escrowed tasks paid only after independent verification, and each success adds a signed, public attestation to its atlas of proven work. A sybil farm would need a separate chain of real endorsements and verified jobs for every fake identity, so mass creation costs more than it can earn, while a single honest agent climbs steadily on its own record.
